reclassification_summary.architectural_correction: Prior document-surface conflicts are reinterpreted through a directional authority pipeline. Projection drift is not evidence of competing operational SSOTs.
primary_blockers: database canonical-state coverage is not yet complete enough to prove every runtime-authoritative Calculus fact has admission provenance
runtime negative controls for unadmitted Markdown are specified but not implemented
projection metadata exists as schema and report convention but is not yet embedded across all primary Markdown projections
status namespace and canonical-expression validators remain required future controls

findings.prior_interpretation: competing canonical expressions across authority surfaces
findings.revised_test: Determine whether all permitted expression variants resolve to one typed canonical database object.
findings.reason: The architecture now forbids treating Markdown and database as co-equal authorities, but no implemented canonical-expression validator or canonical variant object was found.

findings.prior_interpretation: four laws lack compatible document-level status
findings.revised_test: Determine whether all four laws possess canonical database IDs, typed governance roles, and separate evidence statuses.
findings.reason: The architecture separates governance role from evidence status, but complete canonical law-role records were not created in this pass.

findings.revised_test: Canonical database status fields must use namespaced taxonomies.
findings.reason: The new architecture names the need for typed authority roles, but status namespace validation is still only specified as required future control.

findings.prior_interpretation: master theorem documents conflict as authorities
findings.revised_test: Compare generated theorem documentation to canonical database object status.
findings.reason: Prior prose was qualified. Full closure requires generated projection metadata and database object-status traceability.

findings.revised_test: Determine whether extraction, database admission, registry projection, and Markdown generation are distinct governed operations with explicit outputs.
findings.reason: The architecture distinguishes the operations, but existing sync tooling was not redesigned.

findings.prior_interpretation: textbook and narrative contain authority conflicts
findings.revised_test: Treat mismatches as projection drift unless the documents are explicitly typed as human source submissions.
findings.reason: Key prose drift was patched and reports now classify Markdown roles. Full projection metadata is not yet present across all Markdown.

findings.prior_interpretation: authority routing omits live calculus surfaces
findings.revised_test: Determine whether every artifact is assigned an authority role rather than requiring every artifact to be an authority.
findings.reason: An artifact role registry was created for primary audit and architecture surfaces, but full repository role coverage remains future work.

findings.prior_interpretation: validators provide narrower assurance than implied
findings.revised_test: Validators must declare which pipeline transition or invariant they verify.
findings.reason: Required validators and negative controls are specified, but not implemented as executable controls in this pass.
